problem: Existing VLN-CE approaches built on topological and semantic maps use static, offline map construction, which limits scene understanding and adaptation in complex or previously unseen environments.
motivation: Agents in continuous 3D environments must understand unseen scenes on the fly, and static offline maps do not adapt to them. Open-vocabulary segmentation can enrich the map online with language-aligned semantics that link instructions to the scene.
key_idea: Build a vision-and-language map online using open-vocabulary semantic segmentation, then use instruction-driven waypoint prediction on that map and a DD-PPO policy for action decisions.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that an online, open-vocabulary semantic map gives better generalization in unseen environments than static offline maps.
method: Online vision-and-language map construction: uses open-vocabulary semantic segmentation to dynamically build and update a map that enhances scene understanding.
Waypoint prediction module: processes the natural language instruction to identify task-relevant regions, predicts sub-goal locations and guides trajectory planning.
Action decision module: uses a DD-PPO policy to navigate toward the predicted waypoints.
